issues.description: PR bundles three unrelated changes (tests + example behavior swap + README restyle with signature reorder) and should be split.
issues.detail: The diff mixes adding POST tests, swapping req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read() in things_advanced.py, and a sweeping README reformat that includes a real semantic change to StorageError.handle's argument order. These are independent concerns and should be separate patches; the buried signature change is especially risky as a silent ride-along.

issues.description: The stream.read -> bounded_stream.read change is the load-bearing semantic fix but is undocumented.
issues.detail: The one-line swap in things_advanced.py is what actually makes the negative test pass: bounded_stream respects Content-Length so an empty body with a lying header no longer misreads. This invariant (Content-Length is advisory, bounded_stream is authoritative) is never stated in a comment, news fragment, or commit message.

issues.description: New tests only assert status codes and cannot distinguish which guard fired.
issues.detail: resp3 checks 201 without verifying Location or persistence; resp4 checks 400 without identifying whether the empty-body guard, JSON parse, or missing-thing check failed. The tests will pass for the wrong reasons under future refactoring. Assert error title/body and response specifics so the test pins down the protected behavior.

issues.description: FAQ PostTest example is pedagogically muddled and passes by coincidence rather than by stated invariant.
issues.detail: The example complects body-reading with status decisions, uses a redundant 'req.content_length or 0' inside a branch that already excludes None/0, and relies on read-past-EOF returning b'' rather than a stated rule. The invariant being demonstrated (header override semantics) is never written down, so readers cannot tell what the test actually proves.

issues.description: FAQ code sample has style issues: assert-as-function and stray trailing comma.
issues.detail: assert(result.status == ...) reads as a function call but assert is a statement; this is a known footgun and a bad pattern to teach in docs. The one-element list with a trailing comma in headers looks accidental. Match surrounding doc style and prefer 'assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400'.

synthesis.summary: The panel consensus is NEEDS-WORK: the PR bundles three unrelated changes (test additions, a load-bearing stream-to-bounded_stream behavior swap, and a sweeping README restyle that includes a silent StorageError.handle signature reorder) and should be split into separate patches. The actual semantic fix — bounded_stream respects Content-Length, header is advisory — is undocumented despite being the reason the negative test passes. The new tests assert only status codes and cannot distinguish which guard fired, so they protect behavior weakly. The FAQ example is pedagogically muddled, passes by read-past-EOF coincidence rather than stated invariant, and carries minor style issues. Split the patches, document the bounded_stream invariant, and tighten assertions.
